solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The way the present and past PM intimidate is an exercise in elocution

parts.note: how can mean the way or manner in which something is done
now is the present moment
Gordon Brown was a former UK prime minister
to cow is to intimidate or browbeat

explanation.surface: A cryptic description of a politician-themed speech lesson, mixing ways, present and past prime ministers and bullying.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was British prime minister 2007-10.
explanation.definitionFit: This rhyming phrase is the classic drill used by teachers of diction to practise rounded vowel sounds.

clue.text: The man will love this magazine:

parts.note: contracted, the man will becomes he'll
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man promises he will adore a particular magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello! is the name of a British celebrity gossip weekly, so it is an example of a magazine.

clue.text: Cosmopolitan (it's verbose, housing a couple of learners)

indicators.note: housing means the wordy word holds the learner letters inside it
a couple of means the learner letter goes in twice, at two separate points

parts.note: something verbose is wordy
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A sophisticated person or magazine is said to be long-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ls from 'a couple of learners' go in at separate points: WOR-L-D-L-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cosmopolitan is sophisticated and experienced in the ways of society, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Reproductive erotic novel about summertime

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the summertime abbreviation
novel means new, so the letters of erotic are made anew in another order

parts.note: BST is British Summer Time

explanation.surface: A racy book about sex set in the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges EROTIC into OETRIC, which goes 'about' BST (British Summer Time, the UK's daylight saving clock).
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetric medicine deals with pregnancy and childbirth, so it concerns reproduction.

clue.text: Cool maps, all bombs (no shells)

indicators.note: removing the shells of each word strips away its outer letters, leaving the insides

explanation.surface: Military planning documents and munitions, oddly with no ammunition casings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no shells' takes the insides: AP from maps, L from all, OMB from bombs. 'Shells' tempts as ammunition, fitting the bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool as a noun means composure or self-assurance, which is a synonym for poise under pressure.

clue.text: A song which praises trees (promoting the root)

indicators.note: in a down entry the root is the bottom letter, and promoting it moves it up the word

parts.note: palms are trees

explanation.surface: A description of a hymn to trees with roots pushed upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting the root' lifts the bottom S of PALMS (the root of a down light) to just after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred hymn, many of which in the Bible glorify God.

clue.text: Planned car boot sale alas cancelled this month

indicators.note: planned means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order
cancelled means the letters of alas are struck out of the pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad note that the car boot sale someone planned has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ALAS out of CAR BOOT SALE ('cancelled') and rearrange the rest ('Planned'). A car boot sale is a British flea market where people sell from their car boots (trunks).
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle appeared in that autumn month, so 'this month' points to the tenth one of the year.

clue.text: Left cattle in BBC coverage of Lord of the Flies

indicators.note: in places the left-and-cattle letters inside the nickname for the broadcaster

parts.note: the Beeb is the British nickname for the BBC
zebu are humped cattle

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's coverage of William Golding's novel Lord of the Flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord of the Flies' reads as Golding's book but is the literal translation of the devil's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew name of the demon is traditionally translated as the lord of flies, a name for Satan.

clue.text: Endless learning in hand, gripping high street presence

indicators.note: gripping means the hand closes round the shortened learning

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for learning is dropped

parts.note: lore is traditional learning

explanation.surface: Scholarly knowledge held in hand, along with a shop on the main street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts LORE to LOR, which FIST is 'gripping'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower seller is a typical shop found on a British town's main shopping street.

clue.text: Standard rent in arrears, mate

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: in arrears means behind, so the word rent is read from the back

explanation.surface: A tenant behind on the normal rent, addressed as a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in arrears' looks financial but turns RENT backwards to TNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate can be a spouse or companion, a synonym for a partner.

clue.text: Dishevelled Falkland Islanders finally cried after victory

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: wept means cried

explanation.surface: Messy-haired Falkland Islanders wept after winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes D and S, the last letters of Falkland and Islanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair blown about by gales looks untidy, so a synonym sense for messy appearance.

clue.text: Awfully lewd content for Mr Johnson, might start clean-up operation

indicators.note: content for means the scrambled letters become the filling of the politician's name

parts.note: Boris Johnson, former UK prime minister

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of lewd are jumbled
start picks the first letter of might

explanation.surface: Filthy material from Boris Johnson might prompt someone to censor it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges LEWD into WDLE, which is the 'content for' BORIS; 'start' supplies M from might.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Bowdler expurgated Shakespeare, so his name became the word for prudish censorship of text.

clue.text: Rang about extremely fashionable source of news

indicators.note: about means the word for rang goes round the picked letters

parts.note: buzzed means rang, as on a doorbell or phone

indicators.note: extremely takes the letters at both extremes of fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone phoned about an ultra-trendy news outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives FE, the ends of fashionable, and BUZZED goes 'about' them: BUZZ-FE-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: BuzzFeed is an online media company publishing news and viral content.

clue.text: One foots the bill for actor (exit left)

indicators.note: exit is the stage direction for leaving, so the left letter goes out

parts.note: a player is an actor

explanation.surface: An actor leaving the stage left gets stuck with the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exit' removes L ('left') from PLAYER; 'exit left' reads as a stage direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is to pay it, so the person doing so is the one handing over money.

clue.text: Inherently quaint to victimise

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself, intrinsically
cute can mean quaint or charming

explanation.surface: Something charming by nature is set alongside cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute someone is to harass or oppress them, a synonym for picking on them.

clue.text: Outline of French writer

parts.note: de is French for of
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A sketch of a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outline' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline something is to sketch it in words, a synonym for giving an account.

clue.text: Ocean has turned nasty? Right equipment here

indicators.note: turned nasty means the letters of ocean has are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: When the ocean gets stormy, the right gear is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned nasty' looks like weather but signals the rearrangement of OCEAN HAS; the definition leans on the stormy scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue thrown overboard keeps a boat head to wind in a storm, gear for rough seas.

clue.text: See 1 across
See 24
A 21 neighbour, reportedly bitter

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is pronounced to give a word of the same sound

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; 21-down's nationality borders Serbia, so its neighbour is a Serb

explanation.surface: A neighbour of a 21 is described as sour.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer of 21 down; Croatia borders Serbia, so 'a Serb' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare synonym of acerbic, meaning sour or harsh in taste or tone.

clue.text: The last ichthyosaurus not wholly adaptable

indicators.note: not wholly means only part of the words is used, a run of letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: The final surviving marine reptile was only partly flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can change shape and recover, so flexible in a literal or figurative way.

clue.text: See 12
Capital accessible in loose change

indicators.note: in puts the accessible word inside the scrambled letters
loose means free, so the letters of change are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: open means accessible

explanation.surface: Money available in coins in your pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges CHANGE to C...HAGEN, with OPEN 'in' it. 'Capital' and 'loose change' pull towards money.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Denmark.

clue.text: European cormorant's odd features

indicators.note: odd features means the letters in odd positions of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A seabird's strange appearance is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd features' takes letters 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 of cormorant's.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Croatia is a native of a country in Europe.

clue.text: More fool you! Old people finally escape

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A taunt that elderly people at last get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of each word from More to people.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or get away from a pursuer, a synonym.

clue.text: Polish figure of reverence is a cause of conflict when crossed

definitions.text: a cause of conflict when crossed

parts.note: to rub is to polish
an icon is a revered image or figure

explanation.surface: Cleaning a sacred image is a provocative act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' could be the nationality, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's crossing of this river into Italy started civil war, so it stands for a point of no return.

clue.text: He dug Downing St out, expecting match?

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone excavating Downing Street, hoping to find a matchstick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expecting' means pregnant: the marriage is forced by a coming baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding hurried along because the bride is pregnant is the traditional forced marriage of the idiom.

clue.text: 4 score they deployed around soldier in retreat

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the reversed soldier
deployed means arranged in position, so the letters of they are reordered
in retreat means going backwards, so the soldier word is reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Eighty troops deployed around a retreating soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: '4 score' reads like a mark out of ten but is four twenties.
explanation.definitionFit: Four times a score of twenty gives the number.

clue.text: She prophesised the lamentable end of Monte Carlo

indicators.note: lamentable means wretched or bad, so the letters of Carlo are scrambled
end of takes the last letter of Monte

explanation.surface: A seer foretold the sorry demise of Monte Carlo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lamentable' rearranges CARLO to ORACL; 'end of' adds E from Monte.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a priestess such as the Pythia at Delphi delivered prophecies from the gods.
